trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out to (7,4,6) or to (6,6,7) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (7,4,6).
Number 2 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going to (7,6,4) would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going to (6,7,6), the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,6,7). So the line goes to (6,6,7).
Going to (4,6,7) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (6,7,6).

Going to (1,6,6) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (2,7,6).
The line must go to (1,6,6): to (2,7,4) is number 19, which comes later.
Going to (1,6,4) would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (1,4,6).
The line must go to (1,2,6): to (1,4,4) is number 21, which comes later.
Going to (1,2,4), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,2,2); going to (2,1,6) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (2,2,7).
The line must go to (2,1,6): to (4,2,7) is number 10, which comes later.
Going to (4,1,6) would force the line onto number 10 before its turn. So the line goes to (2,1,4).
Going to (1,2,4), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,2,2). So the line goes to (4,1,4).
Going to (4,1,6) would force the line onto number 10 before its turn; going to (6,1,4) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (4,1,2).
I can't rule out to (6,1,2) or to (4,2,1) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (6,1,2).
Going to (7,2,2) leaves no safe move afterwards; going to (6,2,1) would create a bottleneck the line can't pass through in the right order. So the line goes to (6,1,4).
Going to (7,2,4) would cut off a group of 5 cells. So the line goes to (6,1,6).
Cell (4,1,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,2,7).
Going to (7,4,2) would force the line onto number 13 before its turn. So the line goes to (6,2,1).
Going to (6,4,1), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes to (4,2,1).
Going to (4,4,1), the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,4,2). So the line goes to (2,2,1).
Going to (1,2,2) would wall in number 22, the last number. So the line goes to (2,4,1).
Going to (1,4,2) would leave number 13 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (4,4,1).
Going to (4,6,1), the next 10 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 17. So the line goes to (6,4,1).
Going to (6,6,1) would leave number 13 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (7,4,2).
Number 13 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going to number 15 would leave both number 16 and cell (6,6,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (6,6,1).
Number 15 is only reachable this way.
Number 16 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (4,6,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,6,1).
Going to (1,2,2) would wall in number 22, the last number. So the line goes to (1,4,4).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (1,2,4).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
